clue.text: Act indecisively, disheartening digger of trench

indicators.note: to dishearten is literally to remove the heart, so the middle letter of the word goes

parts.note: someone who digs a ditch is a ditcher

explanation.surface: A trench-digger loses heart and cannot make up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' removes C, the central letter of DITCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate and waver, unable to decide what to do.

clue.text: The centre of Bangor, for example?

definitions.text: The centre of Bangor, for example?

parts.words: The centre of Bangor, for example?
parts.note: the middle of a town, read as a town in County Down, since a Bangor is in that Northern Irish county

explanation.walkthrough: Bangor in Northern Ireland is in County Down, so it is a town in Down.
explanation.definitionFit: The central business area of a town is its downtown district.

clue.text: Carry minute symbol representing clan

parts.note: to tote is to carry

explanation.surface: Someone lugs a tiny emblem of their tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as 'tiny' but stands for M, its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem, often an animal, held sacred by a clan or tribe.

clue.text: Discernment musicians need to identify organ with drum

definitions.meaning: a feel for music and pitch
the hearing organ contains the eardrum

explanation.surface: Musicians must spot a particular organ among the drums.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an ear for music is perception of pitch; the ear is also the organ containing a drum.

clue.text: Half-inch Kandinsky painting, for example?

definitions.meaning: rhyming slang for pinch, i.e. to steal or make off with something
Kandinsky was a pioneer of non-representational art

explanation.surface: A tiny measurement set beside a famous modern painter's canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang (a British code where a phrase stands for the word it rhymes with) has half-inch = pinch, i.e. steal; to abstract also means to remove or steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to filch, and Kandinsky's work is the classic non-figurative style of modern art.

clue.text: Person carrying theologian's night-time requirements

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a being is a person or creature
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

explanation.surface: Someone carries a theologian's things needed for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: DD (Doctor of Divinity) stands for a theologian.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding is sheets, blankets and pillows, all needed at night.

clue.text: Uncaring, albeit on time? Not that much

parts.note: albeit means though
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A careless person may be punctual, though not very.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughtless means inconsiderate, showing no care for others.

clue.text: Once on the rocks she was given a starring role

definitions.text: Once on the rocks she was given a starring role

parts.words: Once on the rocks she was given a starring role
parts.note: a mythical princess chained to a sea cliff who was later set among the stars as a constellation

explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the princess was chained to a rock as a sea-monster's victim, rescued by Perseus, and later placed in the sky as a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ethiopian princess of myth was chained on rocks and later became a constellation.

clue.text: Row about a restaurant's opening charges

indicators.note: the word tiff goes around the other pieces

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out over what a new restaurant charges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' takes R from restaurant's; 'about' puts A and R inside TIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a list of charges or prices.

clue.text: Boat turned aside to collect governor on river

indicators.note: to collect is to gather in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: wry means twisted or turned to one side
HE is His Excellency, the title of a governor

explanation.surface: A boat veers away to pick up the governor on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: HE (His Excellency) is the title given to a governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A wherry is a light rowing boat or barge used on rivers.

clue.text: It's OK to swear after this liquid gets spilt

definitions.text: It's OK to swear after this

parts.note: water is the commonest liquid
shed means poured out or cast off, as tears or blood are spilt

explanation.surface: Swearing is acceptable once some liquid has been knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: In British TV the watershed is 9pm, after which strong language and adult content may be broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: The broadcasting cut-off time after which bad language is permitted on television.

clue.text: Leaderless mob beginning to resist system

indicators.note: without its leader, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a horde is an unruly crowd

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A mob without a ringleader starts to resist an established system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' drops H from HORDE to leave ORDE; 'beginning to' takes R from 'resist'.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is a system or arrangement, as in the social order.

clue.text: Languishing in jail like the Vicar of Bray?

definitions.meaning: a prisoner doing a sentence is serving time
the Vicar of Bray, in the old song, changed his beliefs to suit each new monarch

explanation.surface: A churchman from an old song is wasting away in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The Vicar of Bray is the hero of an 18th-century English song who switched religion with every change of ruler to keep his living.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opportunistic, adapting principles to whoever holds power, as the turncoat cleric did; also literally doing a prison sentence.

clue.text: Agriculturist with little grip, possibly

parts.note: small means little
a holder is something that grips

explanation.surface: A farmer with a weak grasp, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' flags that a holder is only one sense of grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A smallholder farms a smallholding, a small piece of agricultural land.

clue.text: Covering answer of stupid person

indicators.note: the word of wraps around the other piece, covering it

explanation.surface: An answer hidden under a cover belongs to a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covering' means OF goes round A.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, dim-witted lout.

clue.text: Fool entertaining top classes? One's naturally jumpy

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: wally is British slang for a silly person
A and B are the top grades or classes

explanation.surface: A fool lets in the best classes, and someone is nervous by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: WALLY is British slang for a fool; 'entertaining' puts AB (the top two classes, A and B) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaby is a small kangaroo-like marsupial that moves by hopping, so it jumps by nature.

clue.text: Sounds like fine linen clothing she washes

indicators.note: signals the words are heard as another word

parts.note: lawn is a fine linen fabric; a garment of it is a lawn dress

explanation.surface: She does the washing of fine linen garments.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawn is a fine linen or cotton cloth; 'lawn dress' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundress is a woman who washes clothes for a living.

clue.text: Understand article in paper, just about

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
about here signals turning the word round

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging name for a newspaper
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone grasps a piece in the newspaper, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just about' turns RAG into GAR; 'in' places THE inside it: GA-THE-R. 'just about' looks like 'approximately' but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather is to infer or understand, as in 'I gather you were there'.

clue.text: Spiritual father swallows liberal medicine

indicators.note: one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: pa is father
a tonic is a medicine

explanation.surface: A priestly father takes a liberal dose of medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts L inside PA, and TONIC follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Platonic love is spiritual, not physical, so the words are close in that sense.

clue.text: How to heat wine, say, and fish

indicators.note: signals the phrase is spoken and heard as a word

parts.note: wine is heated with spices by mulling it

explanation.surface: Instructions for warming wine come alongside a fish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means 'mull it', the instruction for heating wine, sounds like the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A mullet is a type of sea fish, red or grey.

clue.text: Having the will to establish, could one say, a gallery?

indicators.note: set to the gallery's name, placed into it

parts.note: the Tate in London is an example of a gallery
EST is the abbreviation for established

explanation.surface: Someone determined to found what might be called an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: EST (established) goes inside TATE, the London gallery: T-EST-ATE. 'will' looks like determination but is a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes someone who has died leaving a valid legal will.

clue.text: Exist generally to gain mastery

definitions.meaning: to be widespread or current, as a custom does
to triumph or win the upper hand

explanation.surface: Being widespread is the route to dominance.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevail is both to be prevalent everywhere and to win out over opposition.

clue.text: Sick prisoner without head support

indicators.note: old sense of without, outside, so the prisoner surrounds the other piece

parts.note: POW is prisoner of war
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A sick prisoner goes without proper support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: POW goes round ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillow is a cushion that supports the head in bed.

clue.text: Woman leaves filming supervisor for priest

indicators.note: the named piece departs from the longer word

parts.note: a director supervises filming
Di is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman quits as film director to become a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is a woman's name; it 'leaves' DIRECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a parish priest in the Church of England.

clue.text: Leaderless, be likely to stop

indicators.note: without its leader, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be likely to do it

explanation.surface: Without a leader, things are likely to grind to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaderless' removes T from TEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to stop or finish it.

clue.text: Only perfume used by ex-pupil on the way out

parts.note: OB is old boy, a former pupil of a school
sole means one and only
scent is perfume

explanation.surface: A former pupil wears a single perfume while heading out.
explanation.walkthrough: OB, short for old boy, is British for a school's former pupil; the clue gives the pieces in a different order from the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolescent describes something falling out of use, becoming obsolete.

clue.text: Break out dramatically from cooler up tower

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone escapes spectacularly from a jail tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooler' is slang for prison, which feeds the escape picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To erupt is to burst out violently, like a volcano.

clue.text: River plant not wanted on Thames at first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is taken

parts.note: a weed is any unwanted plant

explanation.surface: An unwanted plant grows on the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes T from Thames. 'River' tempts as the Thames itself, but it is the definition of a different river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river on the border of England and Scotland.

clue.text: It's touch and go about circular spelling out policy change

indicators.note: the word abut goes around the other piece

parts.note: to abut is to touch at an edge
O is a circular shape
a turn is a go, as in taking turns

explanation.surface: A circular explaining a change of policy is a risky business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts O inside ABUT to make ABOUT; TURN follows. 'touch and go' reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is a complete reversal of policy or opinion.

clue.text: Origins of this age-old Chinese concept

indicators.note: the starting letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Where an ancient Chinese idea comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'age-old' counts as two words, giving A and O.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tao, or Way, is the central idea of Chinese Taoist philosophy.

clue.text: Daughter with book is unforthcoming

parts.note: to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A daughter who has a book with her is quiet and reticent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like a noun but is the verb, to reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved is reticent and slow to reveal feelings.

clue.text: A writer gets credit, say, for this sort of licence

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe is a writer

indicators.note: signals the word is spoken and heard as other letters

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A writer obtains credit for the freedom a creative piece allows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on tick' is British slang for on credit; 'say' means TICK is heard as TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic licence is the freedom writers take to depart from fact or rules.
